items.title: Howie Shear interviewed by Monk Rowe, Dunkirk, New York, October 11, 2014
items.q: But yet it’s not a dumbed-down version, but’s what players need to know to improvise quite well actually. So it’s not simplified for just like the novice or the grade school kid. It’s really like Charlie Parker played jazz and after him.

ctx.x: And it was an attempt to simplify.

Simplify jazz, yeah. Jazz Improvisation Simplified. Yeah when I was first learning how to play I would go to certain people in the area where I was going to school, before I started school, before I started my master’s in jazz studies. And they couldn’t seem to explain it to me. That’s a lot of the old-timers — at that time they were old-timers. They sort of learned how to play with records. They didn’t have books or academics on how to play jazz. And they didn’t explain it very well. So I said I’d better figure…

then over the years I said I should write a book for my students particularly, and anybody else that wanted it obviously, but to explain all the books that were at a very high level. There were no books that led up to that. And so it’s like learning calculus without learning the essence of arithmetic and the foundations of arithmetic. So I wrote this book and I tried to simplify everything that you would get. But yet it’s not a dumbed-down version, but it’s what players need to know to improvise quite well…
